findings.summary: Paste frame always keeps 200~/201~ markers even if the pane application did not enable DECSET 2004; real terminals send plain text then.
findings.evidence: live S5: cat > f in host shell -> '\x1b[200~붙여 abc\x1b[201~\n'; likely affects sh(dash) fallback and REPLs (inferred)
findings.fix_direction: track per-pane bracketed-paste mode from the pane VT screen (DECSET/DECRST 2004); strip markers when off, keep whole-frame/size rules

findings.summary: Prefix followed by a bracketed paste: ESC consumed as prefix command, '[200~...\x1b[201~' delivered as typed input (lines execute one by one, whole-paste/2 MiB rule bypassed).
findings.fix_direction: when prefix is pending and the next bytes start a paste introducer (or ESC), cancel the prefix (or treat as unknown command) and parse the paste normally

findings.summary: Prefix + non-ASCII key consumes only the first UTF-8 byte; continuation bytes (e.g. \x95\x9c) leak into the pane.
findings.fix_direction: consume the whole UTF-8 sequence after prefix as one unknown command

findings.summary: While help overlay is open, a paste is dropped silently and a >2 MiB PasteRejected sets no notice (C-AC-19 visible reason violated in that state).
findings.fix_direction: handle PasteRejected (and Paste) before the help-close branch: close overlay and either deliver the paste or show a notice
